newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan urges Japanese self-restraint over islands.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan urges Japanese self-restraint over islands.

text.p: Taiwan's Foreign Ministry on Tuesday expressed "grave concern" over a visit by a Japanese legislator to one of a group of disputed islands in the East China Sea, and urged Japan to exercise self-restraint.
"We urge Japan to exercise self-restraint and not to create any trouble that will affect our friendly relations," Foreign Ministry spokesman Roy Wu told a news conference.
"The Republic of China government reiterates its sovereignty over the Diaoyu Islands. This position is unquestionable," Wu said.
The disputed East China Sea archipelago is claimed by Taipei, Beijing and Tokyo.

Shingo Nishimura, a conservative member of Japan's main opposition New Frontier Party, and three other people landed on the Senkaku Islands, known in Chinese as the Diaoyus, on Tuesday to inspect security and hold a brief commemorative ceremony.

Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto was quick to distance the central government from Nishimura's group, which included former cabinet minister Shintaro Ishihara. He is the author of the 1980s nationalist treatise "A Japan That Can Say No".
